1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver I returned these because of a software bug with ANC - and also because the call quality was terrible.

These phones stood out for being wireless with active noise cancellation (ANC) AND pass through (so you can hear ambient sounds for safety in the City). Unfortunately, those features are the weak points of the headphones - to the point that I found I would never use the pass through and often didn't bother with the ANC.

SOUND QUALITY: VERY GOOD - EXCEPT - they tend to exaggerate the mid base a little which can make vocals - especially male vocals sound a little unclear. Listening to the same music on speakers vs the headphones, it was just plane more real sounding and pleasant on good speakers. High standard, I know. Other headphones don't have that particular problem (though may have others - like weak bass or sibilant highs). I haven't heard that many competing models, so I don't know how they compare to sennheiser or bose or anyone else in the same price class. At least others have an app with equalization (Jabra, Jaybird).

Bug w. ANC: Sometimes it would say it's on when it's off and vice-versa.

ANNOYING THING: When you engage the pass-through, it has a voice prompt that tells you the pass through is engaged. Since often I switch on the pass through when it's important to hear something, the several seconds it takes to make its silly announcement means I miss part of what I was trying to hear! I found I would always just yank one plug out of my ear instead and get the instant feedback. ALSO - this thing takes FOREVER to turn off. You have to hold hold hold and finally it announces it's powering off. Combined with poor power indicator light - this is just annoying.

NOTE: This is not a defect, but just poor design... There is NO WAY to activate Google Assistant or Siri with These. Even my cheapo earbuds let you use one of the buttons to summon Google. Without that, how are you supposed to make voice calls? I have to pull out my phone to make calls. Foo.

Combined with atrocious call quality (I could hear them, but the person on the other end is always mishearing words or saying WHAT? WHAT?), these are DOA for me.

ONE LAST THING: The APP is garbage. Just pointless.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Targus Demolition Backpack Designed to Fit up to 17.3-Inch Laptop, Black (TSB220US) I was able to do a direct comparison between this and the SwissGear SA1908 ScanSmart Backpack. And it turns out that deciding which pack to grab on the way out is surprisingly one of the hardest decisions one could have to make. Both packs are obviously of the best quality with a similar nylon shell, strong stitching, and smooth zippers. Both are designed to fit 17" laptops and have similar interior volumes, and yet the features vary widely. Let's have a look at key points:

-The Targus is perfect for a user carrying a laptop and a tablet and/or Kindle. In front of the laptop compartment is a soft fabric lined pocket to hold a tablet against the laptop and protect the screen from scratches. The very front pocket is also soft with a piece of padding that fits the newest Kindle nicely.

-The SwissGear may be better for carrying just a laptop or two laptops. It has the ScanSmart feature, which is great when TSA allows it to work (sometimes they make you remove your computer anyway, either out of ignorance or their suspicion that you packed incorrectly for it to work - that makes it easier just to remove it sometimes rather than risk a fight with them). And I often store a second laptop in the ScanSmart opening.

-I love that on the Targus, the zipper pulls for the main compartment and the two side compartments can be placed between the bag and your back, thwarting casual thieves. As an extremely paranoid person, this gives extra peace of mind. For that matter, I really like the unique design of these pockets. The side pockets can be really useful, and the big compartment can be accessed from a larger opening. But that uniqueness comes at a cost...

-...and that cost is the looks. I didn't like the looks on the picture, but then it grew on me. In person, I don't really like it that much, but it might be growing on me. I guess the tradeoff is simple: you get a very unique design that works great and you get some serious padding for your electronics and some extra comfortable straps, but that all equals a slightly awkward looking pack. It's not too bad, but I think an accent color would go a long way. In contrast, the SwissGear under observation is quite beautiful and more traditional, yet not as padded or protected.

-The Targus came in a very thin box. It has a semi-rigid pad on the bottom that can fold up to flatten it out or fold down and attach with velcro to add some structure to the main compartment. This is also a very smart feature.

-The SwissGear has a phone/MP3 player holder with earphone exit, for those interested. That's not the best one I've ever seen though, as it is only a hanging cradle for the device.

-The Targus has more padding, while the SwissGear has a better airflow system for your back.

Conclusion: I really love both of these backpacks, and I'm surprised how different two top notch backpacks can be. I can see how the designers have to pick and choose the features they want to incorporate, because you really just can't have it all without making the pack bigger, and I wouldn't want that. They both deserve five stars, absolutely. The Targus strikes me as the pack for someone serious about the transportation and protection of their electronics, or anyone else who is intrigued to try this unique, excellent design.
text_fidelity_b: Targus Demolition Backpack Designed to Fit up to 17.3-Inch Laptop, Black (TSB220US)

text_fidelity_a:
PDP Gaming Universal Media Remote – PlayStation 4, TV After countless times of the ps4 controllers dying on me due to short battery life, media use on the ps4 was beginning to be a bit of an annoyance. Thankfully, the PDP universal ps4 remote has come to the rescue; well, for the most part. First and foremost, let me say that for the price, it does everything it needs to do and does it well. All of the buttons feel solid and are easy to use, the construction is good, the back is nice and grippy, it is lightweight and because it is a universal remote, it also works on your TV and other electronics. When attempting to use it with my TV it quickly synced itself without issue however I should note I have a Sony television.
If you are looking for a basic remote for Blu-ray movies and Netflix, this is it. It completely solved the battery issue I had with the ps4 remotes, as it has not died on me once. If you are a Hulu user however, you can stop reading, it simply isn’t good enough for Hulu as it can behave somewhat erratically and will not go out of Hulu menus once in them. Outside of Hulu however I have not had a problem with the controller and it functions great with anything else I may need.
There are some minor issues with the remote, for example in order to change the volume you have to switch to the TV controls and then switch back to the ps4 to work with that. It may have just been my controller, and it was easily worked around (use both controllers) but some may find that an issue. When price is factored in, I would say that for the most part, the small annoyances are just that and most users will be able to overlook them. If I had to give a star rating it would be a 4 out of 5 star product. Half a star off for lack of Hulu compatibility and another half off for the little kinks it still has, overall a good product.
text_fidelity_b: PDP Gaming Universal Media Remote – PlayStation 4, TV

text_fidelity_a:
Datacolor Spyder5EXPRESS – Designed for Hobbyist Photographers (S5X100) I ended up using this colorimeter to profile and calibrate my monitor. Out of the box I was not very happy with the quality of the product. You end up getting pretty much zero instruction and no manual. I had to figure it out on my own just by looking at the product. Once that annoyance was over I got to experience how terrible the default software from datacolor is.

I looked to the reviews and decided I could make the most of this purchase by using other free calibration software. I used Argyll and DispCalGUI. If you simply download DispCalGUI it will prompt you automatically to download the Argyll color libraries.

You then go into Tools->Instrument->install Argyll CMS instrument drivers...

This will download the drivers you need to run the spyder 5.

After this calibration is possible. I calibrated and it seemed to do a decent job. All in all, the calibration software looked like it was powerful--certainly better than the default.

In the end, I returned the product. I wanted something that would work without me having to go the extra mile to get it to work. At this point, with all of the extra I had to do to calibrate I still don't know if it did a good job or not.

Dimensions can be seen in the photos I have attached.

Included is the unit only.

Pros:
*Calibrates
*Decent price

Cons:
*Terrible OEM software (-2 stars)
*Setup--while not hard--is not immediately obvious. A small pamphlet would have gone a long way (-1/2 a star)

Additional Considerations:
Go for hardware that has good software calibration tools. You cant beat the two working in synergy.

Overall: 2.5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 3 stars

If you have any further questions regarding the product in my review please leave a comment below and I will get back to you as soon as possible.
text_fidelity_b: Datacolor Spyder5EXPRESS – Designed for Hobbyist Photographers (S5X100)

text_fidelity_a:
myCharge PowerGear Sound Protective Portable Charging Case for Wireless Earbuds Headphones | Custom Tray Compatible with Powerbeats & Removable for Other Brands | 1400 mAh / 1A Output The MyCharge is a handy if not tiny clamshell charging case for PowerBeat headphones, though it will work for others as well.

Pros:
The case itself has an hard outer shell that feels durable and thick. I have no fears the earbuds will be well protected inside. It opens and closes easily and tightly. As much as a case can be, it’s aesthetically pleasing—a dark, slick black with a black ribbon with red stitching running down the middle (the red stitching matches the red inside). The ribbon/band does more than add a bit of style and color; it also gives it a bit more texture so it grips the surface it’s atop better.

The plastic tray inside is designed for the PoweBeats line, so the earbuds nestle snugly (but with no need to wrestle or force them in) into an indentation so they lie flat and with a mid-section to insert the connecting wires/controls into. It’s a good fit, well-designed, and I don’t feel like I’m overstressing the wires, though I wouldn’t want to leave them in that position for a long amount of time (though I tend to worry about that sort of thin more than others)

It comes with a cable. You can use any one, but you’ll want it to be very short

The port to charge the case (the battery inside the case for sticklers) is easily accessible.

An LED on the front lets you know if the case battery is getting low

Cons
I wish the port cover felt a little more durable

Mixed or Up in the Air
I haven’t had it long enough yet to check how many charges, but I’ve gotten a few without a noticeable impact on the case battery. I don’t know if their promise of a dozen-plus will bear out, but I don’t think it’ll be far off if not.

The case isn’t really tiny (You can see the dimensions above). If you’re looking for something to slip into a pocket, then this will be a con, though it will easily fit a coat pocket. It will fit cargo pockets but you’ll definitely know it’s there. On the other hand, it doesn’t take up a lot of space, it’s quite protective, and if you’re worried about losing your expensive but very small and easy to lose earbuds, putting them in a noticeable, protective case that will also charge them back up is far from the worst idea. Personally, I’m OK with the size.

As noted, the case is designed for PowerBeats, so your mileage will vary on how well it fits some other type. My other earbuds all fits in the case without an issue, just not as snugly or neatly. That isn’t a real priority for me even ignoring the fact that I have PowerBeats.

Overall, a good value for what it does I’d say.

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft EKZ-00001 Modern Keyboard with Fingerprint ID I use laptops at home instead of tower systems, but I still prefer a stand-alone keyboard for most things. I have had very good success with Microsoft peripherals in the past so I had high expectations for this keyboard. So far, it works well enough but I have encountered a couple of snags that make it less than perfect.

This is a slim and efficiently designed keyboard and it is slightly wider than my 15.6” laptop. It’s the right size for me and I am happy with the dimensions when it comes to fitting it in my work space. No complaints there.

Set-up is a little on the tricky side. I tried to set it up for Bluetooth use without following the instructions first and got nowhere. It does not appear in the list of available devices so it could not be paired right off the bat, though my system does handle the Bluetooth standard. The instructions say to connect it via USB first, then turn it on and follow the set-up when Windows detects it. However, the instructions do not say that you must use the cable that came with the keyboard; I used a different one and failed, though the keyboard did work as a USB keyboard with that 3rd-party cable connected.

I’ll answer the very obvious question right now – I was able to get it working under Linux as a USB keyboard, but not as a Bluetooth keyboard. I am not sure if the problem is with the Bluetooth receiver in the system I tested or if the keyboard is just not compatible at all. I have an iPhone as well and it did not see the keyboard in the list of available devices. This is not a failure or a shortcoming of the keyboard – it operates very much in accordance with how it has been marketed, so getting it to work under Linux with Bluetooth would have been just a bonus. Interestingly, it says it can be set up to work under the Windows Phone platform which has been discontinued...

When I set it up under Windows 10, it did not go as the documentation said it would go. I did get the toast notification and I clicked as directed. It set everything up and said it was ready to go. It never allowed me to set up the fingerprint configuration and I have been unable to find any setting within Windows to allow me to revisit. So, I have a fingerprint reader that I can’t configure. Considering that this is being used in a home with a private computer with password protection this really isn’t a show-stopper but it would have been nice to mess with this technology.

In operation the keyboard is very responsive and so far I have been pleased with it except for one thing that I cannot seem to reconfigure. I prefer to have the function keys operate as function keys by default, instead of media keys. Without being able to find a keyboard configuration setting in the OS anywhere I have no way to reverse the default operation, which is to require pressing the Function key prior to hitting F1 – F12 to get them to default as function keys instead of media keys.

I do like this keyboard and it works well for my needs. The set-up isn’t bullet-proof though, and there are some behaviors it would be nice to change or reconfigure.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft EKZ-00001 Modern Keyboard with Fingerprint ID

Transcend 16 GB Class 6 SDHC Flash Memory Card TS16GSDHC6 I have been using Panasonic SDHC Class 6 4GB cards, and have been pretty happy with them. I decided to get this one just because of the low price and high ratings, and am pleased to find that I agree with the many 5-star reviews.

Some information I didn't see in the other reviews, in case it's of interest: I ran a write test with a big file on my computer, and saw write speeds consistently above 6MB/s, as you ought to expect for a Class 6. (Among other things, that means of course that your camera can get ready for the next shot just that much faster because it's spending less time waiting for the recording to be completed.)

I didn't bother with a read test, since read speed is rarely an issue.

A comment on SD card readers/writers. As many have said, older SD devices, including older cameras, will not work with SDHC cards. My old card adapter (Sandisk 8-in-1) hung when I put this chip in. But my newer adapters (a built-in slot, and an Edge All-in-1) worked just fine. So if you're having trouble, this is possibly the first thing to check.
text_fidelity_b: Transcend 16 GB Class 6 SDHC Flash Memory Card TS16GSDHC6

Otium Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.0 Headphones with Digital Intelligence LED Display 3500 mAH Charging Case 135H Playtime Stereo Sound Headset IPX8 Waterproof Built-in Mic for Home Office… Great ear buds, and they arrived super quickly as well!

The ear buds come with a charging case, usb charging cord, several size ear pieces, and the ear buds themselves.
The charging case comes almost all the way charged, mine was at 98% upon delivery, and the ear buds were also fairly well charged at about 80%. They're held in the case with magnets, which is nice for storage and piece of mind, knowing they will stay put while charging. The charging case can actually be used as a power bank for your phone/mobile device too, which is pretty awesome! I didn't realize this at purchase, so it was a nice bonus.

After fully charging both for first time use, the buds will auto pair with each other when taken off the charging case. They paired very easily with my galaxy s9, and I was actually pleasantly surprised by the sound quality.
They touch sensitive area on the ear buds is most of the outer area shown when put into your ear, so be sure to get the situated first, and then turn your music on to avoid awkward on/off mishaps while putting them on.

The instructions included are very clear. Left ear is long hold volume down, right is long hold volume up, skipping tracks back or forward is quick press of either ear. Answering and ending calls can be done from either ear also.
These can also be used in single ear mode (using the left as the "master" pod), and will auto switch to the right pod as master if the left dies, so you can continue single ear use while charging the left.

Overall these are very nice little ear pods for a great price. If you are shopping around, I absolutely recommend buying these!

LifeProof NÜÜD SERIES for iPad Pro 9.7" (ONLY) - Retail Packaging – BLACK This is my first Lifeproof.

Pros. Feels light compared to the Ottobox Defender on my Air 2. A very nice feel to it. Yes it makes it bulky, but not heavy. That was a big surprise. I didn't weigh the two, and the specs indicate the Defender and Lifeproof weigh about the same, but it just feels better in my hands than the Defender. The Defender does have a stand though.
Very easy to install and uninstall. Lifeproof provides a plastic key to open the case easily. Simple but wonderful.
Reasonable protection. I have the Apple Smartcover and Smartcase on my 12.9 IPad Pro. I like it. It's very light, has a stand, but does
not offer much in the way of protection. It's also very expensive, for what it is.

Cons. I was shocked that it does not have a screen protector. On the plus side, not having a screen protector maximizes enjoyment of the screen. Nothing to peel off either. If you add a screen protector, you increase the risk of leakage. If water isn't a concern, then add a screen protector. A stand feature would have been nice.

Other: The directions say to perform a water test before the first use, every 3 months, and before an expected water inflow, such as boating. A you tube video was very helpful. Otherwise, I would have thought I was missing a screen protector. There are some good amateur videos demonstrating an IPad Air installation. Same process.
text_fidelity_b: LifeProof NÜÜD SERIES for iPad Pro 9.7" (ONLY) - Retail Packaging – BLACK
